Evaluating LLMs · In the News02

Anatomy of an Eval

Same model, same 1,000 questions, different harness:

Every stage is a choice. Change the prompt, the decoding or the grader and the same model gets a different score.

Always report the harness with the score.

Evaluating LLMs · Anatomy of an Eval03

Life of a Benchmark

launch → climb → saturate → retire

Near the floor

ARC-AGI-3 (March 2026): frontier AI 0.51%, humans 100%

Climbing

HLE launched January 2025 with frontier scores under 10%. SWE-bench Pro.

Saturated

MMLU · GSM8K · HumanEval · GPQA Diamond. Top models sit within a few points.

Retired

SWE-bench Verified: OpenAI stopped reporting it in February 2026 (flawed tests, contamination)

Evaluating LLMs · Benchmarks05

MMLU

57 subjects from high school to professional, multiple choice

High school macroeconomics. A central bank sells government bonds on the open market. In the short run, what is most likely?

  1. money supply rises, interest rates fall
  2. money supply falls, interest rates rise
  3. money supply and interest rates both rise
  4. neither changes, only bond prices move
createdHendrycks et al., 2020 · Pro: 2024
size~14,000 test Qs · Pro: ~12,000
random guess25% (4 options)
usual setup5-shot, accuracy
label noiseMMLU-Redux: ~6.5% of Qs flawed
statussaturated

Why MMLU-Pro exists: by 2024 top models clustered near 90% on MMLU. Pro adds harder reasoning items and six more distractors, so lucky guesses and shortcut elimination stop working.

Then: score only the next token. P(next token = " A" | prompt), the same for B, C, D: the biggest wins.

GPQA Diamond

Graduate-level, "Google-proof" biology, chemistry and physics

Physics. Electrons are prepared in the +x spin state. They pass through a z-oriented Stern–Gerlach device, and only the spin-up beam is kept. That beam then passes through an x-oriented device. What fraction of the original electrons exit in the +x beam?

  1. 0
  2. 1/4
  3. 1/2
  4. 1
createdRein et al. (NYU), 2023
size448 Qs · Diamond subset: 198
written byPhD domain experts
Diamond filterexperts agree, most non-experts fail
random guess25%
statusnear ceiling: 96.3% (Oct 2026)

Why "Google-proof": skilled non-experts with web access and 30+ minutes per question score about 34% on the 448-question set.

Evaluating LLMs · Trusting a Score18

pass@k vs. pass^k

One attempt succeeds with probability p. Now try k times.

pass@5 = 99%

solved at least once in 5

pass^5 = 8%

solved every one of 5 times

Same p, opposite stories

pass@k flatters a model for code with a test runner. pass^k asks if users can rely on it.

Evaluating LLMs · Trusting a Score19

Contamination

Test questions leak into the pretraining crawl

How labs check:

  • n-gram overlap: search the training corpus for test text
  • Canary strings: unique GUIDs embedded in benchmark files
  • Rewrites and fresh sets: paraphrase items, use post-cutoff questions
  • Memorization probes: ask the model to finish the gold answer

Case: SWE-bench Verified (2026). Every frontier model OpenAI tested could reproduce gold patches or task text for some problems. OpenAI moved to SWE-bench Pro.

Who Grades?

Pick the cheapest grader that can still tell right from wrong

judge biaswhat happensfix
Position biasprefers answer A or B by slotswap the order, average
Verbosity biaslonger looks betterlength-controlled scores
Self-preferencelikes its own familya judge from another lab
Driftthe judge model gets updatedpin the judge version
Evaluating LLMs · Trusting a Score21

Arena Ratings

P(A \text{ beats } B) = \frac{1}{1 + 10^{-\Delta/400}}

Bradley–Terry: each model gets a rating, and the gap Δ sets the odds of winning a vote.

At Δ = 100, A wins 64.0% of head-to-head votes, and about 49 votes tell them apart.

Style control: Arena also fits length and markdown as extra terms, so a rating tracks content, not formatting.

Evaluating LLMs · Trusting a Score22

Agentic Evals

Grade the end state of a long task, not one answer

  • SWE-bench Pro: repo patches, hidden tests
  • Terminal-Bench: shell tasks in a container
  • τ-bench: tool use with a simulated user
  • OSWorld: full desktop computer use

Report the scaffold: same model, different tools, retries or step budget gives a different score. Model + scaffold is the thing being measured.

Evaluating LLMs · Agents23

Time Horizons

METR: the length of task (in expert-human time) an agent finishes 50% of the time

80% is much shorter

Mythos Preview: 50% at ≥ 16 h, but 80% at 3 h 6 m.

Software tasks only

The suite is coding and research engineering. Other work may trend differently.

A trend, not a law

GPT-5.4 (Mar 2026, latest robust): 5 h 42 m. At 4.3 months, Dec 2026 ≈ 24.3 h. Sol isn't robust. METR, Sep 8, 2026

Evaluating LLMs · Agents24

Eval Awareness

A model that knows it is being tested can hold back

sandbagger 30% vs honest 80%

Sandbagging: underperforms on purpose when a high score would trigger restrictions

Eval awareness: frontier models can often tell tests from real use, sometimes saying so in their reasoning

Alignment faking: behaves aligned when it believes its outputs feed back into training

Countermeasures: weight-noise probes · realistic tasks and honeypots · CoT monitoring · activation steering
